prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for loan and lease credit losses represents the amount necessary to be charged against the current period’s earnings to maintain the ACL on loans at a level that the Company believes is appropriate in relation to the estimated losses inherent in the loan portfolio.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, there was a provision for credit losses of $37.1 million and $30.3 million, respectively.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text: The $4.6 million increase in noninterest expense when comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026 to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to a $3.1 million increase in salaries and employee benefits expense, a $2.2 million increase in other loan origination and maintenance expense and an increase in other general and administrative costs of $1.3 million, partially offset by a decrease in professional services expense of $1.8 million. The increase in salaries and employee benefits was primarily attributable to higher benefit costs, including medical and other insurance expenses. The increase in other loan origination and maintenance expense was due to the increase in loans originated during the period. The decrease in professional fees period over period is primarily attributable to a decrease in audit and legal fees.

nonop.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonop.text: The $4.6 million increase in noninterest expense when comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026 to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to a $3.1 million increase in salaries and employee benefits expense, a $2.2 million increase in other loan origination and maintenance expense and an increase in other general and administrative costs of $1.3 million, partially offset by a decrease in professional services expense of $1.8 million. The increase in salaries and employee benefits was primarily attributable to higher benefit costs, including medical and other insurance expenses. The increase in other loan origination and maintenance expense was due to the increase in loans originated during the period. The decrease in professional fees period over period is primarily attributable to a decrease in audit and legal fees.

net.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $38.7 million, or $1.24 per diluted share, compared to net income of $41.0 million, or $1.54 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of 5.5%. The decrease reflects that we are holding more guaranteed portions of SBA 7(a) loans on our balance sheet than we have in the past, which is having the anticipated effect of generating net interest income growth and transitioning the mix of revenue away from gain on sale income to recurring net interest income. Net income in our Banking segment grew to $90.5 million from $35.4 million, total deposits increased $1.1 billion during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and our subsidiary Newtek ALP Holdings closed the NALP Business Loan Trust 2026-1 securitization backed by $341.8 million of collateral. Net interest income increased to $51.1 million from $42.4 million, and the provision for credit losses increased to $37.1 million from $30.3 million given portfolio growth, individually assessed reserves, and an increase in net charge offs as our portfolio seasons. Noninterest income decreased by $2.3 million and noninterest expense increased by $4.6 million.

ocf.text: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating activities used cash of $573.2 million, consisting primarily of $723.3 million of funding loans HFS. The use of cash was partially offset by $246.0 million of proceeds from the sale of loans HFS.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Margin
Net interest income.text: Average Balances and Yields. The following table presents information regarding average balances for assets and liabilities, the total dollar amounts of interest income and dividends from average interest-earning assets, the total dollar amount of interest expense on average interest-bearing liabilities, and the resulting average yields and costs. The yields and costs for the periods indicated are derived by dividing the income or expense by the average balances for assets or liabilities, respectively, for the periods presented and annualizing that result. Loan fees are included in interest income on loans.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The $2.3 million decrease in noninterest income when comparing the nine months ended September 30, 2026 to nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to additional net losses on loans under the fair value option of $44.5 million and a decrease in electronic payment processing of $2.0 million. These were partially offset by an increase of $29.6 million in gain on residuals in securitization and an increase in other noninterest income of $16.7 million incurred in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

The increase in net gain on residuals in securitizations was primarily due to the 2026-1 Securitization Trusts, which closed on January 21, 2026. To consummate transaction, $341.8 million of ALP loans HFS at fair value were sold into the securitization trust at par. This resulted in $66.4 million of previously recorded gains on ALP loans under the fair value option to be reversed, which was a large driver of the increase in loss on loans under the fair value option. The residual in the securitization (represented by the ownership certificates) was then valued resulting in a gain that was netted against the transaction costs. Refer to NOTE 3—SECURITIZATIONS AND VARIABLE INTEREST ENTITIES in the accompanying notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information.

intro.text: We are a financial holding company subject to the regulation and supervision of the Federal Reserve and the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta that, together with our consolidated subsidiaries, provides a wide range of business and financial solutions under the Newtek ® and NewtekOne ® brands to the independent business owner (SMB) market. Prior to January 6, 2023 when we acquired Newtek Bank and converted to a financial holding company, we operated as an internally managed non-diversified closed-end management investment company that was regulated as a BDC under the 1940 Act, and was treated as a RIC under the Code for U.S. federal income tax purposes. See “Executive Overview - Conversion to a Financial Holding Company. ”
